subject: Re: Proposed MAP & staging plan for Brightline (private offer + staged commit)
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@brightline.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & timeline proposal for Brightline evaluation

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Tom and I walked away excited about the latency profile and the prefix caching story. Procurement looped me in and asked for a Mutual Action Plan that ties evaluation milestones to commercial checkpoints (pricing signals, commit thresholds, and ramp cadence).

Can you share a MAP draft that maps evaluation activities (POC criteria, 2-week load test, security signoff) to the commercial steps for a private offer on AWS Marketplace? Our procurement is specifically asking for:
- A staged commit model (trial -> 6-month pilot -> annual commit)
- Pricing bands and discount triggers based on sustained qps/volume
- Expected ramp timeline and rollback/fallback options if SLA targets aren't met

We'd like something we can circulate internally by next Thursday (26th).

Best,
Sara

Sara Lopez
Head of Platform Partnerships, Brightline Analytics

Attachments: none
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@brightline.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for Brightline evaluation

Sara — thanks, and appreciated the clarity on procurement's needs. I attached a first-pass MAP and a pricing staircase PDF. High-level summary here and next steps below.

Quick summary (see attachments for the matrix):
- Phase 0 (Discovery, 1 week): baseline telemetry collection; no charge beyond demo credits.
- Phase 1 (POC, 2-3 weeks): sandboxed evaluation with test workloads; we recommend a 2TB token cap for the pilot — standard hosted SKU, 20% evaluation discount.
- Phase 2 (Pilot/ramp, 6 months): staged private offer on AWS Marketplace. Pricing bands that unlock at 30% and 70% of committed qps (examples in PDF). We propose a 6-month pilot commitment of $100k with a 10% credit applied toward the annual if converted.
- Phase 3 (Annual commit): multi-region private offer with committed spend and SLA credits. Deeper discounts (15–25%) when customers commit to reserved capacity and cross-region replication.

Critical commercial signals tied to MAP milestones: acceptance of POC results triggers private-offer issuance, pilot kickoff triggers first tranche of committed billing, and 70% sustained utilization over 60 days triggers higher discount band. We include explicit rollback language (auto-fallback to hosted) if latency SLOs drop below 95% for a 14-day rolling window.

Next steps:
1) Review attached MAP matrix and pricing staircase.
2) Tell us which pilot commit size you want modeled (we used $100k as an example).
3) If optics look good, we'll generate an AWS private offer draft and a preliminary DocuSign term sheet for Brightline legal.

I've looped in Priyom for pricing calibration and Karthik for marketplace/commit mechanics.

Cheers,
Diego

Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.xlsx, pricing-staircase-3-tier.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for Brightline evaluation

Diego — quick notes on the pricing side:
- The $100k pilot is fine as a modeling anchor. For Brightline's projected qps, recommend we tier pricing per million tokens with the following sample bands: baseline $X / unit, 30% volume discount at $X1, 70% discount at $X2. (Details in the PDF and spreadsheet)
- Suggest we include a 60-day utilization window to trigger the next discount instead of 30 days — reduces churn risk.
- For AWS private offers, we can stage three commitment tranches (pilot, scale, steady-state). Each tranche converts into reserved capacity SKUs that the runtime can pin.

Karthik — can you confirm technical constraints on creating a staged private offer with multiple tranches? Also we should pre-populate a marketplace SKU set so the customer sees per-SKU unit pricing in the AWS console.

—Priyom

Priyom Das
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@brightline.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for Brightline evaluation

Sara / team — quick operational note from the marketplace side:
- AWS supports private offers that can be staged, but the conventional pattern is a single private offer with optional amendment windows. To represent tranches we'll create three SKUs (pilot, committed-6mo, annual) with linked discounts and billing profiles.
- We'll provide a Marketplace test link you can use during the POC so procurement can see the private offer UI.
- Need the exact legal entity name and billing address for the private offer. Sam in Marketplace ops will also require a short statement of work attached to the offer.

Sara — if you share the legal entity and preferred pilot commit number (we used $100k in the MAP), I'll push a draft private offer to AWS and share the secure link.

Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@brightline.ai>, Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@brightline.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for Brightline evaluation

Sara / Tom — great, thanks for the quick review and for confirming the internal timeline. Per your ask, we: 
- Updated the MAP spreadsheet to include a 60-day window for discount triggers and explicit go/no-go checkpoints at each milestone.
- Modeled the pilot at $100k and attached a version that shows alternate $75k and $150k tranches.
- Created the AWS private offer draft and uploaded it to the Marketplace test environment: https://marketplace.aws.amazon.com/privates/offer?id=PF-789123 (shared link, preview-only).
- Laid out the DocuSign term sheet (preview link above) that includes rollback language and SLA credit mechanics.

Next actions for Brightline:
1) Confirm legal entity and billing address for the private offer (required for AWS).
2) Decide which pilot commit size you want modeled (75k / 100k / 150k).
3) Share an internal owner for the POC who we can schedule a 2-week load test with.

If you confirm by EOD Monday 30th, we can have the private offer sent to procurement for signature by end of next week and start the pilot the first week of December.

Cheers,
Diego
